title: Measuring _C. elegans_ food intake in liquid culture
protocol: Inoculate 5 mL of LB containing 100 μg/mL Ampicillin and 0.1 μg/mL Amphotericin B with a single OP50 colony.
Incubate the culture for 8-12 hours at 37°C in a bacterial shaker.
Dilute the OP50 culture 1:2000 in 300 mL TB containing 50 μg/mL Ampicillin.
Incubate the diluted culture overnight at 37°C until saturation is reached, not exceeding 14-16 hours.
Transfer the saturated OP50 culture into a pre-weighted sterile centrifugation tube.
Centrifuge the OP50 for 10 minutes at 3500 rpm (2200 x g).
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend the pellet in sterile water.
Repeat washing the pellet twice with sterile water.
After the second wash, carefully remove all remaining water from the tube.
Weigh the centrifuge tube containing the OP50 pellet and subtract the weight of the empty tube to determine the weight of the pellet.
Thoroughly re-suspend the pellet in S-complete to a concentration of 100 mg/mL.
Use a photometer to determine the number of bacteria per mL if necessary.
Adjust the concentration of the OP50 feeding solution to 2 x 10^10 bacteria/mL as needed.
Store the adjusted OP50 solution at 4°C until use for worm culture.
Transfer animals to a fresh plate on day -6, Friday at 4:00 p.m.
Sterilize a metal spatula by heating it over a Bunsen burner.
Let the spatula cool.
Use the cooled spatula to cut out agar chunks from the plate containing starved worms.
Transfer several of these agar chunks onto a fresh 10 cm NGM plate seeded with OP50.
Incubate for approximately 65 hours at 20°C until the majority of the worm population consists of gravid adults.
Collect worms from the 10 cm NGM plate by washing them off the plate with 5-10 mL sterile water.
Transfer the worms/water solution into a 15 mL conical tube.
Wash the worms by centrifuging for 30 seconds at 2000 rpm.
Discard supernatant and add 10 mL of water.
Repeat washing until the solution containing worms has largely cleared of bacteria.
Remove the supernatant and add 5 mL of freshly prepared bleach/NaOH solution (1.8 mL household bleach, 0.5 mL 10N NaOH, 7.7 mL water).
Incubate for up to 5 minutes at room temperature until the worms break open.
Vortex gently every minute during incubation.
Monitor the progress of the reaction under a dissecting microscope.
Do not over-bleach worms as larval viability will be severely diminished.
Reduce bleach time or NaOH concentration if viability becomes an issue.
Add 5 mL of M9 buffer to neutralize the reaction.
Centrifuge the eggs/debris solution at 3000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and add 10 mL of M9 buffer.
Vortex the solution briefly to dissociate the egg pellet.
Repeat the M9 buffer wash twice.
Wash the eggs once with 10 ml S-complete and transfer the solution to a fresh 50 mL conical tube.
Add 30 mL of S-complete to achieve a final volume of 40 mL.
Gently shake the tube overnight at room temperature on a nutator or similar device.
Check under the dissecting scope whether the worms have hatched during the night.
Determine the concentration of worms in the S-complete solution by counting the number of worms in 10 μL drops using a dissecting scope.
Count at least 10 drops for each sample.
Resuspend each worm strain to a final concentration of 40 worms/mL in S-complete.
If measuring lifespan or stress-resistance, use concentrations up to 75 worms/mL.
Prepare a no worm control solution containing Carbenicillin, Amphotericin B, and OP50 in S-complete medium.
Add Carbenicillin to the final concentration of 50 μg/mL.
Add Amphotericin B to the final concentration of 0.1 μg/mL.
Gently shake the solutions on a nutator at room temperature until animals are ready for plating.
Add OP50 to a final concentration of 6 mg/ml (1.2 x 10^9 bacterial cells/ml).
Transfer 150 μl of worm/OP50 solution into each well of a 96-well plate with a transparent bottom, ensuring worms are in suspension during pipetting.
Transfer 150 μl of no worm control solution into the wells of a 96-well plate with a transparent bottom.
Seal the plate using tape sealer to avoid contamination and evaporation.
Shake the plate on a microtiter plate shaker for 2 minutes.
Incubate the plate for 2 days at 20°C until the animals reach the L4 stage.
Sterilize animals by adding Fluorodeoxyuridine (FUDR).
Add 3-4 μL of FUDR stock (6 mM) to each well to achieve a final concentration of 120 μM.
Re-seal the plate using tape sealers.
Shake the plate for 2-3 minutes on a microtiter plate shaker.
Return the plates to the 20°C incubator.
Add 0.5 μL of a 300X stock to each well for DMSO soluble drugs.
Add 0.5 μL of DMSO or Drug/DMSO solution to control wells for DMSO soluble drugs.
Add 3 μL of a 50X stock to each well for water-soluble drugs.
Add 3 μL of Water or Drug/Water solution to control wells for water-soluble drugs.
Seal the plates with tape sealer after adding drugs.
Shake each plate for 2-3 minutes on a microtiter plate shaker.
Check for dead animals using an inverted microscope.
Shake each plate on a microtiter plate shaker to dissolve bacterial aggregates and re-suspend bacteria into solution.
Shake each plate on a microtiter plate shaker for 25 minutes.
Measure the OD600 for each well using a microplate reader capable of measuring optical density at 600nm.
Complete all OD600 measurements within 10 minutes after shaking.
Save output files for later use.
Return plates to the 20°C incubator.
Shake each plate on a microtiter plate shaker for 2 minutes before counting worms.
Count the number of live adult animals in each well using an inverted microscope with a 2x or 2.5x objective.
Record dead and live animals using the attached excel template FeedingAssay.xlsx.
Allow fresh oxygen to enter the culture by removing the tape sealer.
Wait 1 minute.
Reseal the plate.
Shake the plate for 2-3 minutes on a microtiter plate shaker.
Repeat once every week.
Add new OP50 on Day 5 to prevent starvation when performing a lifespan assay.
Measure the OD600 after adding new OP50 if food intake and lifespan measurements will be performed on the same animals.
Ensure that new OP50 is also added to the control wells.
Censor wells containing more than 15 adult worms from analysis.
Censor wells with fewer than 3 adult worms for increased reproducibility.
Censor any wells where hatchlings are observed.
Measure the change in OD600 over time for each condition or treatment.
Count the number of worms per well.
Determine the basal decay of OD600 for bacteria in the absence of worms.
Calculate the difference in OD600 between Day 4 and Day 1 for each well.
Establish the basal decay of OD600 for each treatment condition by measuring in control wells as described in Section B 10c and Section C 2/3.
Calculate the ΔOD600 for each well in each set of controls.
Determine the average decay \(D_c\) for each set of control wells.
Use \(D_c\) as a correction factor for experimental wells with the same drug and solvent combination.
Subtract the appropriate average basal decay value from the difference in OD600 per well.
Divide the result by the number of worms per well to calculate food intake per well.
Normalize the food intake values for each condition relative to an appropriate control, using untreated Bristol N2 strain as a standard control.
